title: Coles a la Burguesa (Cabbage Bourgeoise Style)

Remove the leaves one by one and place a little filling on each
Reassemble the leaves one on top of another as if the cabbage were whole

title: Coles Rellenas a la Francesa (Cabbage Stuffed French Style)
description: Prepared with beef, ham, and egg yolks.
steps: Parboil two medium cabbages for twenty minutes in boiling salted water
Refresh in cold water, let drain, and remove the core
Chop half a pound of beef and one pound of fatty ham, seasoning with salt, whole pepper, a little cilantro, cumin, ginger, saffron, cinnamon, clove, black pepper, all ground, and grated nutmeg
Mix in seven or eight egg yolks and use this mixture to stuff the cabbages, tying them very well
Line a cooking vessel with ham slices and add some parsnips, onions, and a mixed herb bundle, placing the cabbages on top and moistening with undefatted broth
Cook over low heat for an hour and a half
Drain the cabbages afterwards, press them slightly to squeeze out liquid, untie, and serve with Spanish sauce underneath

description: Prepared with apricots, syrup, and orange juice.
steps: Boil water in a pot with two handfuls of soda

Wash them well and prick with a pin
Place in cold water
Return to boiling water to blanch them and remove from heat
Wrap in cloth, place in cold water, and drain on a sieve
Leave covered and give them one boil in clarified syrup
Remove from heat and leave in the syrup for one or two hours

title: Compota de Peras Encantilladas y Rellenas (Candied and Filled Pear Compote)
description: Prepared with pears, ground almonds, and custard.

ingredients.name: Bergamot pears, ripe and without cloves
Sugar, six pounds, clarified and strained
Custard without composition, two to three cuartillos

steps: Select ripe bergamot pears without cloves, peel them and hollow them out, removing the core and more
Weigh the pears to make six pounds and place them in warm honey and water made with six pounds of clarified and strained sugar
Boil for two or three hours, then set aside and keep for the next day, repeating the same operation the following day and again on the third day
On the third day, when they have boiled a little, bring the honey to half point and remove the pears, placing them on a platter to drain
To the honey remaining in the pot, add one pound of ground almonds and two to three cuartillos of custard without composition, allowing it to reach the point of cajeta
Cover the pears with this mixture after filling them with coconut paste
Place the platter on the ground, leaving it hollow so it does not burst, and form a tlecuilli with bricks or stones on top
Place a comal with heat on top so it browns on the upper part

title: Condumios de Cacahuate (Peanut Candies)
description: A confection made with peanuts and sugar.
steps: Heat clarified syrup made from sugar to the soft-ball stage (punto de juntar en el agua)
Add the ground peanuts to the syrup

Place the mixture over the fire and bring it to the cajeta stage
Remove from heat and beat the mixture
Pour onto a wooden board (cajón) before it sets completely

title: Conejo en Caldo Colado de Lentejas (Rabbit in Lentil Sauce)
description: A sauce made with rabbit, broth, and ham.
steps: Divide the rabbit into pieces and cook in good broth with lean ham, an assorted herb bundle, and black pepper
Cook lentils separately in unsalted broth with some onions browned in butter
When the lentils are cooked, pass them through a sieve with their broth
Remove the rabbit and ham from their cooking broth and decrease the broth by incorporating it with the lentil puree

title: Conserva de Zanahorias Encantadas (Enchanted Carrot Preserve)
description: A fruit preserve made with carrots, honey, and almonds.

ingredients.name: Honey (3 cuartillos for every 3 pounds of carrots)

steps: Scrape the carrots with a knife and cut them to the desired size, removing very well all the core without breaking or opening the tubes
Weigh them and keep them boiling in water for one hour
Remove from the water little by little with a skimmer, place in a small basket and cover with a cloth so they cool
Boil three cuartillos of honey for every three pounds of carrots
Once the honey is skimmed, strained and cold, pour it over the carrots that have already been strained in a pot, placing it over a moderate fire of wood and not charcoal
As soon as the carrots are well soaked and the honey reaches the proper point, remove the pot and take out some of the honey, which should be given another boil separately in a small pot
Add peeled and toasted almonds cut into small pieces and other pieces of walnuts and pine nuts, all toasted in advance
Give another boil immediately, taking care that the honey does not burn and that everything is well mixed and soft like an alfajor
Sprinkle this with orange flower water and dust with cinnamon, ginger, and cloves, all ground

steps: Boil three quarters of milk in a saucepan
Add a small amount of green lemon rind, which can be taken with three fingers of coriander, a small piece of cinnamon and five ounces of sugar with two grains of salt
Continue boiling until the milk is reduced to half
Let cool a little
In another saucepan, dissolve a small amount of flour, about a scant coffee spoonful, in six egg yolks
Pour the cream there little by little, stirring at the same time

description: Prepared with fish, garlic, and vinegar.

Drain well from the oil and let cool
Grind the golden garlic and dissolve it in plenty of good vinegar, adding a little ground pepper and cloves
Heat the vinegar with bay leaves, plenty of thyme, Chinese oregano, about two orange leaves, slices of limes and lemon peels and rinds
After one or two boils, heat oil and fry the vinegar with all that has been added, then set aside

Let them puff up well, remove them still hot

title: Empanadas (Meat Pies)
description: A pastry dish made with lard, wine, and yeast.

ingredients.name: some yeast dissolved in salted water

steps: To 1 pound of melted and cooled lard, add 1 small cup of water with salt, 1/4 cuartillo of generous wine, and some yeast dissolved in the salted water, beating everything together until incorporated.
Gradually add flour, mixing until the dough is soft and can be extended.
Place the dough in a lard-greased bowl and cover it.
If the dough is made in the morning, make the empanadas in the afternoon; if made in the afternoon, make them the following morning.
Extend the dough with a rolling pin on flour dust, cut to desired size, and fill with picadillo, adding pieces of ham and cooked egg, olives and chiles in quarters.

For fish versions: fry onions, garlic, tomatoes, and chopped green chile in lard, then add a little water (if not using catfish), salt, cooked fish pieces proportioned to the empanadas, saffron, cloves, and ground pepper, chopped parsley, oil, and vinegar, simmering until reduced.
In each empanada place a bit of the sauce, a piece of fish, some capers, olives, and chopped chiles (if small empanadas) or quarters of chiles or whole chiles (if large ones).
Fold and crimp the edges with the thumb all around.
Dampen the edges with a little water to seal well and press the top onto the bottom.
Beat an egg (yolk and white) and brush the entire upper surface with a feather.
Place on tin sheets and bake in a well-tempered oven until cooked and dried, then sprinkle with sifted sugar.

title: Empanadas de Pescados (Fish Empanadas)
description: Prepared with fish, lard, and lemon.
steps: After the fish is cooked, remove bones and spines
In a pan, put a little lard and oil, a few drops of lemon, plenty of tomato, chopped onion and garlic
Place to fry adding clove, cinnamon and pepper
Once fried, add the fish and one tablespoon of the broth in which it cooked
Let it boil a little and set aside to cool
Knead one pound of fine flour with hot water and salt dissolved in the water
Add two raw eggs and a little lard, well kneaded
Wrap in a cloth for a while, then extend with a rolling pin so it is not too thin
Place the fish in the center and fold the other dough over, cut it giving it the shape of an empanada, crimping the edge so the broth does not escape
Coat a baking pan with lard, place a paper larger than the empanada and this is placed on the paper and put over two violent fires so they cook quickly and the dough does not become hard
Once done, sprinkle with sugar or sesame before serving

title: Empanadas Hojaldradas con Azúcar y Vino (Puff Pastry Empanadas with Sugar and Wine)
description: A pastry dish made with wine, sugar, and egg yolks.
steps: Place one pound of flour on a table and add five egg yolks, wine, salt, a little butter, a small amount of sugar so it is not too sweet, and sufficient water to mix and knead
After kneading well, extend with a rolling pin
Spread butter on it and fold in half

Place on papers on baking sheets
Bake in the oven

title: Empanadas para Piezas Grandes (Empanadas for Large Pieces)
description: Prepared with yeast, lard, and wine.

ingredients.name: 1 pound of melted and cold lard

steps: Dissolve a little yeast with a cup of salted water
Mix with one pound of melted and cold lard and three servings of Málaga wine or other generous wine
Beat until all is well incorporated
Gradually add flour in the necessary quantity so the dough becomes smooth and can be extended, kneading at the same time
Place this dough in a lard-greased bowl and cover for eight to ten hours rest
After this time, extend with a rolling pin on a table sprinkled with flour
Cut empanadas to the size needed to cover the fish or piece to be placed in it, or cut small portions for small empanadas
Fill with minced meat, fish, or recado alone
Placing what they are to contain in the center, fold and crimp the edges
Shape gracefully and variously, imitating with the dough the fish or piece contained inside, or other animals or flowers

description: Prepared with lard, powdered sugar, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: half a pound of powdered sugar
filling: minced recado, blancmange, or other milk sweet

steps: Place in a bowl one pound of lard, half a pound of powdered sugar, five egg yolks, and corresponding salt
